questions.explanation:
1) Structured Clinical Risk assessment HCR-20 (Webster): It is a popular structured clinical assessment tool for violence risk. HCR-20
(Historical, Clinical and Risk) shows good inter-rater reliability. It has 10 historical items (history of previous violence, PCLR score etc), 5
Clinical items (lack of insight, diagnosis of PD) and 5 risk management items (feasibility of plans, lack of support etc). It has been useful in
predicting inpatient violence and community violence in discharged patients.

questions.emi_instruction: Choose the most likely data pertaining to epidemiological observations for the following statements:
questions.question_text:
What percentage of homicide perpetrators with a history of 'mental disorder' has personality disorders as a primary
diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
All of the required data to answer this EMI can be found in "Avoidable Deaths' - �ve-year report of the national con�dential inquiry into
suicide and homicide by people with mental illness. www.nmhdu.org.uk/silo/�les/avoidable-deaths-�ve-year-report-.pdf
Among all homicide perpetrators, 30% have one or other mental disorder mentioned in the psychiatric reports, with around 10% having had
a contact with mental health services in the last 12 months. Interestingly schizophrenia, alcohol /substance use and a�ective disorders are
equally prevalent (18% each, of all those 30% with a 'diagnosis'), but the most common diagnosis is personality disorders (27%). In essence,
5% of all homicide perpetrators have a diagnosis of schizophrenia and another 5% have personality disorders as the primary diagnosis. Of
the 5% perpetrators with a personality disorder, 29% had been in contact with services in the last 12 months, 28% had been in contact but
not in the last 12 months and 43% had no previous contact with services at all. In total, 55% of the perpetrators with a PD had a secondary
diagnosis, mainly alcohol and drug dependence. 92% of those with PD as a primary diagnosis are imprisoned, while 4 % receive hospital
disposal. On the other hand, 29% of those with schizophrenia were imprisoned while 71% received a hospital order. In total, around 6% of
homicide perpetrators receive a hospital disposal. Women and >65 age group are more likely to receive this outcome after a homicide.
Among these, 70% have schizophrenia or related illnesses.

questions.explanation:
Sugarman & Walker adapted the HONOS scale by adding 'SECURE' items to enable its use in secure forensic settings. HONOS-Secure was
previously known as HONOS-MDO. The 7 security rating items include risk of harm to adults or children; risk of self-harm (deliberate or
accidental); need of building security to prevent physical escape; need for a safely sta�ed living environment; need for escort on leave
(beyond the secure perimeter); risk to individual from others and the need for risk management procedures. HoNOS-secure is not a risk
assessment tool, but a tool that enable the clinical risk assessment to be translated to need for care and clinical risk management.  
DUNDRUM is a structure professional risk assessment tool to guide decisions regarding placement in forensic services. It de�nes eleven
items relevant to the decision to allocate a person to high or medium security, low security, open hospital beds or community follow-up.  
HCL-R focuses on psychopathic traits  
Ref: Flynn, G., O'Neill, C., McInerney, C., & Kennedy, H. G. (2011). The DUNDRUM-1 structured professional judgment for triage to appropriate
levels of therapeutic security: a retrospective cohort validation study. BMC Psychiatry, 11(1), 43.

questions.emi_instruction: Using the most widely accepted epidemiological data, identify the probabilities associated with each of the following scenarios
questions.question_text:
Proportion of prisoners that will self-harm
during their prison term
questions.explanation:
Around 90% of shoplifters, when convicted, will not reo�end. The remaining 10% will repeat the o�ence.  
Self-harm is much more prevalent among prisoners than among the general population. One-half of female remand prisoners have self-
harmed at some time in their lives and more than one-quarter in the previous year. The corresponding �gures for men are about half of
these. Perhaps as many as 10% of prisoners will self-harm during their term with the likelihood increasing with the length of time in custody.
Highest rates are among sentenced female prisoners who have spent two or more years in prison, 23% of whom will have self-harmed
during the current term (Meltzer et al., 1999).
A national clinical survey of people convicted of homicide (n=1594) in England and Wales (1996-1999) showed that (34%) had a mental
disorder: most had not attended psychiatric services; 85 (5%) had schizophrenia (lifetime); 164 (10%) had symptoms of mental illness at the
time of the o�ence; 149 (9%) received a diminished responsibility verdict and 111 (7%) a hospital disposal - both were associated with severe
mental illness and symptoms of psychosis.  
Ref: IShaw, J., Hunt, I. M., Flynn, S., Meehan, J., Robinson, J. O., Bickley, H., ... & Appleby, L. (2006). Rates of mental disorder in people convicted of
homicide. The British Journal of Psychiatry, 188(2), 143-147.
